alternatives.description: Keep ProcessVersion 1.4 expressed separately across workflow prompts and existing evolution primitives without a shared process engine.
alternatives.projected_effect: The admitted process remains valid, but route/state semantics are duplicated across executors and are harder to test as one contract.
alternatives.risk: Implementation drift can arise when lanes independently encode route transitions or gates.

alternatives.description: Implement one abstract GardenProcess state machine, composition-based gate policies, ProcessFactory, and six sibling route implementations using existing evolution/algebra validators.
alternatives.projected_effect: Common route/state semantics become executable and centrally testable while scheduled lanes remain role executors rather than process-definition owners.
alternatives.risk: A faulty abstraction could centralize an implementation error, so exact ProcessVersion binding, route-specific tests, algebra conformance, and external authority gates must remain load-bearing.

bidirectional_gaps.gap: DO_NOTHING lacks one executable route/state contract and central Process Algebra transition validation.
The engine introduces a shared implementation dependency that must remain synchronized with admitted ProcessVersion 1.4 and cannot replace external authority or conformance gates.

assumptions: GardenCanonicalUpdateProcess@1.4 is the HUMAN-admitted current governing process.
Garden v15.5 remains the immutable canonical design baseline.
The engine implements admitted process semantics and does not create new canonical Garden semantics.
Process Algebra validation is conformance evidence only and cannot grant authority or prove complete semantic compliance.
MAJOR_DELEGABLE and MAJOR_PROTECTED must remain sibling route implementations so protected authority cannot leak through inheritance.
reason.uncertainty: This implementation does not yet prove every ProcessVersion 1.4 rule is ENFORCED/AUDITED/RE_VERIFIED; later RuleEnforcementCoverage must measure that maturity explicitly.
counterexamples: A process transition that uses an unregistered Process Algebra operator must fail.
A LIGHT route entering semantic admission would violate the route table.
A protected MAJOR promotion that succeeds without external HUMAN protected-decision evidence would be invalid.
An algebra receipt that mints authority or claims semantic compliance would be invalid.
A cycle bound to ProcessVersion 1.3 must not be silently executed as ProcessVersion 1.4.
reason.conclusion: Implement the composable process engine as implementation/conformance infrastructure, retain all external authority and admission boundaries, and validate each runtime transition against the registered Process Algebra profile.

obligations.statement: All six admitted ProcessRoute classes resolve to concrete process implementations while preserving route-specific forbidden transitions.
Runtime process transitions use only registered Process Algebra operators and acknowledge registered non-laws.
MAJOR_PROTECTED cannot inherit delegable promotion authority and still requires external HUMAN protected-decision evidence.
The process engine cannot mint authority, admit a semantic delta, or promote Garden canon merely by validating a transition.

items.claim_scope: Explicit instruction to implement the parent/abstract process architecture and require Process Algebra compliance.
Declares the composable engine architecture, route implementations, algebra binding, tests, and non-authorizing boundary.
Provides the executable registered Process operators and required non-law acknowledgements.
